critique.good: The term column keeps individual terms intact and makes the row identifiers easy to scan. Headers are clear, and the two prose columns remain associated within each bordered row.
critique.problems: Definitions form tall, narrow blocks, while examples often finish much earlier, leaving substantial empty space within rows. The example column also wraps into many short lines.
critique.cause: The 120px term column is just wide enough for its longest word, leaving 135px for definitions and 104px for examples. Both prose columns are constrained, but the longer definitions drive most row heights.

critique.good: The wider definition column produces more readable phrases and shorter rows. Examples also have a little more room than in r0A.
critique.problems: Several row identifiers visibly break inside words, including Idempotency, consistency and Backpressure. That damages the first column's primary scanning function, despite the reported split count.
critique.cause: At 95px, the term column provides only 74px of text width, less than the 99px needed by its longest unbreakable word. The extra definition width comes at the expense of intact identifiers.

critique.good: The wider example column gives examples more natural phrases and makes them easier to read across from the definitions.
critique.problems: Term identifiers and long definition words visibly split, and definitions become very tall stacks of short lines. Examples frequently end far above the bottom of their rows, weakening the visual balance between the companion columns.
critique.cause: The 110px term column provides 89px of text width, below the 99px needed, and the 120px definition column provides 99px, below its 108px longest word. Giving 129px to examples leaves too little space for the longer definitions.

critique.good: The term column is easy to scan, headers stay on one line, and words remain intact. The wider definition column gives the longer prose a useful advantage; this is the most compact of the three renders.
critique.problems: Definitions still form tall, narrow blocks, especially in CAP theorem. Examples often finish much earlier, leaving large empty areas within already tall rows.
critique.cause: At 135px, Definition has only 114px for text. Example has 83px, enough to keep its longest word intact but too little for comfortable prose; the 120px term column also leaves substantial unused space below short labels.

critique.good: The 109px example column makes some examples less cramped, while the term labels and headers remain clear and words stay intact.
critique.problems: Definitions become more fragmented, with noticeably taller rows for Eventual consistency, Backpressure and CAP theorem. The extra example space does not compensate for the loss of definition width across the table.
critique.cause: Reducing Definition from 135px to 130px leaves 109px for text, barely above its longest unbreakable word. Small changes in line breaks add several lines to long cells.

critique.good: The term column preserves clear row identification, and the prose stays within the viewport without mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The wider term column gives little visible benefit over r1A, while definitions wrap more and several rows grow taller. Examples remain as narrow as in r1A.
critique.cause: Moving 2px from Definition to Term leaves Definition at 133px and Term at 122px; the extra term width does not prevent the multiword labels from wrapping.

critique.good: The bold term column supports scanning, and the wider definition column gives the longer prose priority. Row borders keep each definition and example associated.
critique.problems: The example breaks “consecutive” across lines in the Circuit breaker row. The narrow prose columns also produce tall rows and leave substantial empty space beneath many examples.
critique.cause: The 103px example column leaves only 82px for text, just short of the longest unbreakable word. The 120px term column preserves the longest term but leaves limited width for both prose columns.

critique.good: All words stay intact, headers fit, and the term column remains easy to scan. The example has a little more room, improving its line breaks and making it a better companion to the definition.
critique.problems: Definitions remain very narrow and fragmented; the Quorum row becomes taller than in r2A. Long rows and uneven amounts of white space make cross-row scanning laborious.
critique.cause: Increasing Example to 105px avoids the word split, but reducing Definition to 134px gives it only 113px of text width.

critique.good: The wider definition column improves several line breaks and shortens the first and last data rows. The hierarchy and row boundaries remain clear.
critique.problems: “Backpressure” splits in the term column, damaging the key scanning label; “consecutive” also splits in the example. The shorter table comes at the cost of word integrity.
critique.cause: The 119px term column leaves 98px for a 99px word, and the 103px example column leaves 82px for an 83px word.

understanding.purpose: Define distributed-systems terms and illustrate each with an example.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the first column for a term, then read across its row to connect the definition with the example. Wrapped lines should remain easy to associate with their row.
groups: Definition and Example are companion prose columns: one explains the term and the other makes it concrete.
Term is the row identifier and needs enough prominence to support scanning.
keep_intact: Individual words and technical identifiers, especially long terms and unbreakable words in the prose.
The association between each term, its definition and its example.
may_wrap: Multiword terms can wrap between words.
Definitions and examples can wrap naturally at word boundaries; longer cells can absorb additional lines in the other cells of the same row.

bad.why: The example column splits “consecutive” across lines, interrupting the sentence for a small gain in definition width.
The row label “Backpressure” splits mid-word, weakening the term a reader needs to find and identify.
The example column splits “consecutive” across lines, while the unused pixel could prevent the break.

final.rationale: r2B and r3A keep the row labels and prose words intact while giving the longest column, Definition, the most space. Their rows have the same heights and very similar wrapping, so the one-pixel exchange between Definition and Example does not produce a meaningful visual advantage. The term column remains wide enough for “Backpressure,” and the shaded row headers keep each long entry identifiable.

general: Protect row identifiers and unbreakable words when allocating narrow columns.
Give width according to each column’s reading role and content, while judging the resulting rows as units.
A shorter table is not an improvement if it introduces distracting word breaks.
specific: The term column needs about 120 px to keep “Backpressure” intact.
An example width of 103 px splits “consecutive” in the supplied renders; 104 px avoids that split.

final.tradeoffs: The wider example column in r1B and r3B gives examples more breathing room, but leaves definitions more fragmented and makes the table taller. A designer might accept the isolated example-word split in r2A for its shorter table.
final.uncertain: The ranges describe the tested preferred allocations, not a verified continuous interval: changing one column requires adjusting the others to stay within 359 px, and other nearby combinations were not rendered.

A.why: The term and definition columns scan reasonably well, but the narrow example column breaks 'consecutive' across lines and makes examples choppy.

B.why: Terms remain intact and examples read reasonably well, though the narrow definition column creates many short lines and a lengthy table.

C.why: The nearly equal columns split 'Backpressure' and long definition words across lines, weakening both row identification and reading flow.

D.why: Terms and long words remain intact, and the definition has useful space. Examples still wrap into short lines, but rows remain easy to associate.

E.why: The definition has room for relatively natural phrases, terms remain intact, and examples avoid the mid-word break visible in A. The narrow columns still make rows tall.

F.why: The columns preserve terms and long words while giving the definitions useful space. Examples are narrow but legible, and the row structure remains clear.

reviews.unsure: D, E and F are close; their small width differences make the choice sensitive to individual line breaks. All are constrained by the phone width and have tall rows.

A.why: The near-equal columns leave the definition cramped and split words, including the row label Backpressure. Long rows contain substantial empty space beside the definitions.

B.why: Row labels remain intact and the definition has more room, but the narrow example column produces many short lines and an uneven distribution of white space.

C.why: The wider definition column improves the densest text and keeps row labels intact, but the example column splits consecutive across lines.

D.why: Row labels and words remain intact, while the definition has enough space to read reasonably well. Examples are still narrow and require frequent wrapping.

E.why: The columns keep labels and words intact and give the definition more space than the example. Both prose columns remain narrow, making rows tall.

F.why: The compact labels leave room for the longer definition, and words stay intact. The example column is narrow but remains readable.

reviews.unsure: D, E and F are very close; their small differences in wrapping do not produce a clear overall winner. All three involve substantial wrapping at this viewport width.
